hook: I saw a road accident. If I **help the victim**, will I get into trouble?
hook_q: What happens if I help an accident victim?

slides.title: The law **protects** you.
slides.body: If you help an accident victim in good faith, you are legally protected from civil or criminal liability.

slides.title: You don't have to **give your name.**
slides.body: No police officer or any other person can force you to share your name, identity, address or other personal details. You may share them if you choose to.

slides.title: Being a witness is **your choice.**
slides.body: If you volunteer as a witness, you may be examined once, at a time and place convenient to you.

slides.title: At the hospital, **remember this.**
list: Hospitals cannot demand payment from you for emergency care
Once the patient is admitted, you are free to leave
Detention by authorities is not permitted
You can get a confirmation that you brought the victim

slides.title: Treated with **respect.**
slides.body: You must be treated respectfully, without discrimination on grounds of religion, nationality, caste or sex. Every public and private hospital must display a charter of your rights in Hindi, English and the local language.

slides.title: You may even get **₹25,000.**
slides.body: Under the Government's Rah-Veer scheme, a person who helps a victim of a serious road accident get medical attention within the Golden Hour (the first hour after the injury) can be eligible for ₹25,000 and a Certificate of Appreciation.

sources: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 – Section 134A (inserted by MV (Amendment) Act, 2019) (via PIB)
Central Motor Vehicles Rules – Good Samaritan Rules, GSR 594(E) dated 29 Sep 2020 (via PIB)
PIB (MoRTH): 'Rules published for protection of Good Samaritans' (1 Oct 2020); 'Rah-Veer: Save a Life Without Fear' (4 Jan 2026)
caption:
Scared to help at a road accident? The law is on your side. 👇

1️⃣ Helping an accident victim in good faith? You're protected from civil or criminal liability
2️⃣ No one can force you to give your name, address or other personal details
3️⃣ Being a witness is your choice. If you volunteer, you may be examined once, at a time and place convenient to you
4️⃣ Hospitals cannot demand payment from you for emergency care, and you're free to leave once the patient is admitted
5️⃣ Help a serious road accident victim get medical care within the Golden Hour and you can be eligible for a ₹25,000 Rah-Veer reward

Source: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (Sec 134A); Good Samaritan Rules, 2020 (GSR 594(E)); PIB (MoRTH)
